newsitem.title: USA: U.S. budget deal economically neutral -- Raines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. budget deal economically neutral -- Raines.

text.p: The new U.S. budget deal will not over-stimulate the economy, White House Budget Director Franklin Raines said Tuesday.
"The agreement is neutral and in the later years it actually restrains consumption because it is reducing the size of the government as a percentage of gross domestic product," Raines told CNBC.
Reducing the size of the government sector would allow for greater expansion of the private sector, Raines said.

When asked about the budget outlook beyond the five-year horizon of the current plan, Raines said progress needed to be made now on Social Security and Medicare reform to avoid a ballooning budget deficit as Baby Boomers retire.
"That will go a long way to helping us keep this budget in balance," he said.
